title: Chiral Floquet Selection of an Algebraic Rydberg Bound State in the Continuum
authors: X. Z. Zhang, X. F. ZHang, M. W. Liu
abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) remain localized despite the presence of extended modes at the same energy. In driven systems with long-range couplings, the absence of radiation does not by itself determine how a bound state decays in space. We study a Hermitian Rydberg spin waveguide coupled to a four-site plaquette, where a winding drive phase combines rotation with time translation to forbid propagating guide channels in one symmetry sector. The resulting eigenstate remains embedded in the continuum of other sectors and carries an inverse-cube waveguide amplitude, with coherent contributions from direct plaquette--guide coupling and long-range guide propagation. Pair-state calculations determine the microscopic couplings in the axial geometry, while coherent Floquet mixing sets the weight of the dominant circulating plaquette mode. The bound state thus retains the spatial signature of the long-range coupling even when radiation is forbidden.
summary: This paper analyzes the existence and properties of an algebraic Floquet Bound State in the Continuum (BIC) within a Rydberg waveguide coupled to a plaquette. By applying Floquet theory and symmetry analysis, the authors demonstrate that the bound state retains a characteristic inverse-cube spatial decay signature even when symmetry forbids all radiative decay channels. This confirms the robustness of localized quantum features in complex, driven quantum architectures.
main_problem: The study investigates how a bound state embedded in the continuum (BIC) maintains its spatial localization signature when its radiation channels are forbidden by symmetry in a driven system.
main_result: The system supports an algebraic Floquet BIC whose nonradiating waveguide amplitude decays as $n^{-3}$, confirming the persistence of long-range coupling signatures even when radiation is symmetry-forbidden.
method: The analysis employs Floquet theory, Green's function techniques, and Feshbach projection methods to separate the bound state response from the continuum of propagating modes.
model_or_system: The model is a Hermitian Rydberg spin waveguide coupled to a four-site plaquette, driven by a winding phase. The system is analyzed in the Floquet framework to study quasienergy eigenstates.
key_observables: Nonradiating waveguide amplitude decay exponent ($\alpha \approx 3$), the static unwanted-channel ratio ($\eta_{C4}$), and the state overlap ($O_{ax}$).
important_parameters: Winding drive phase, transverse displacement ($\delta$), and the guide length ($L_w$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the guide is semi-infinite for asymptotic decay calculations and relies on symmetry conditions to forbid propagating guide replicas.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how Floquet symmetry separates radiation from the bound response, detail the algebraic decay of the nonradiating amplitude, and show the quadratic onset of symmetry-breaking effects ($\eta_{C4} \propto \delta^2$) upon transverse displacement.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the BIC concept in driven systems, calculating the guide response using Green's functions, quantifying the algebraic decay exponent, and finally analyzing the robustness of this state against symmetry-breaking perturbations via transverse displacement.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical understanding of how topological or symmetry constraints can enforce robust, localized quantum states (BICs) in open, driven quantum systems, which is highly relevant for designing robust quantum emitters or waveguides.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Floquet symmetry separates radiation from the long- range bound response. (a) A winding-driven C4 mode belongs to a joint sector whose accessible guide replicas are gapped even though other sectors form a folded continuum; the non- propagating coupling remains long ranged. (b) The axial static channel has ℓs = 0, and phase-factor order r = 1 couples to the angular component ℓeff = −1. (c) The complete state, including its waveguide component, is nonradiating because no propagating guide replica is available in its κ = 2 sector, while its bound guide component obeys qm = (Em −Hw)−1fm. An embedded eigenstate must also satisfy the real self-consistent eigenvalue equation.

FIG. 2. Spectral proximity and algebraic localization of the same Floquet branch. (a) Periodic quasienergy distance ∆ext to the waveguide-like extended subset for the single-tone and bi- harmonic drives. (b) Plaquette weight, target-chirality weight, and IPR of the single-tone branch. (c) Lw = 321 snapshot amplitudes for both waveforms and the geometrical reference Kgeo, each normalized at n = 108; colors and markers follow panel (a). (d) Amplitude exponents fitted in interior window WB, with whiskers spanning windows WA–WC of Supplemen- tal Material, Sec. VIII. The guide has open ends and uses Ω/J∗= 1.21, z1 = 1.1, and z2 = 0 or 0.1.

(a) A transverse displacement produces a quadratic onset of the unwanted-to-target static angular-channel power ratio ηC4; the dashed line fits the small-displacement regime. (b) Schematic view of the 25-atom geometry, with the four-site plaquette enlarged for visibility. (c) At the axial point, the direct ARC exchange has a finite ℓs = 0 component while the ℓs = ±1, 2 components vanish to numerical precision. (d) The finite Floquet branch remains continuously connected to the axial state over the plotted displacement range.
